children: The handset maker is targeting the sub-Rs 20,000 smartphone segment while reportedly exploring a Rs 500–600 crore fundraise

Lava International Managing Director Sunil Raina and Chief Financial Officer Rajesh Sethi are set to step down from their respective roles by December, as the Indian smartphone maker looks to secure fresh capital and revive business growth. Co-founder Hari Om Rai, who stepped down as managing director in 2023, has returned to the role.

A company spokesperson confirmed the departures, saying that Raina and Sethi had decided to move on from their positions. Sethi was acknowledged for his contributions to the company’s financial operations and business priorities.

According to reports, both executives have submitted their resignations and are serving their notice periods, with their exits expected by December. Raina is reportedly leaving to pursue business ventures outside Lava.Raina joined Lava in 2010 as Vice-President and Chief Marketing Officer before moving through several senior positions. He took over as interim managing director in November 2023 after Rai was arrested by the Enforcement Directorate in a money-laundering case linked to Vivo. Raina was formally elevated to managing director in June 2025.

Sethi joined Lava as Group Chief Financial Officer in May 2024. Before joining the handset maker, he worked with Iraq-based Ster Group and held positions at Bharti Airtel, Telenor Group and Essar Group.The latest departures follow the exit of Sanjeev Agarwal, who served as Chief Manufacturing Officer and later as Executive Director and Chief Manufacturing Officer at Lava.

The leadership changes come as Lava seeks to strengthen its position in the smartphone segment priced below Rs 20,000. The company has previously said its smartphone business grew by 60–70 per cent during the year, despite a contraction in the overall market.The sub-Rs 20,000 segment represents an opportunity for the company as it seeks to revive growth and expand its market presence.

Lava is also reportedly exploring a fundraise of around Rs 500–600 crore to finance expansion and potentially restructure part of its debt.Earlier reports have suggested that promoters of electronics manufacturers Dixon Technologies and Amber Enterprises are in discussions to acquire stakes in Lava in their personal capacities. The reported discussions and fundraising plans come as the company navigates leadership changes and seeks fresh capital to support its next phase of growth.
